params.why: unequal legs keep the instances varied (the isosceles case is the book's own special triangle)
coprime legs keep the hypotenuse root already in simplest form
the hypotenuse must be a genuine surd, not a whole number (excludes the 3, 4 pair)

stem: In the right-angled triangle $ABC$ the right angle is at $B$, $AB = {=p}$, $BC = {=q}$ and $AC = \sqrt{{=N}}$. Let $\theta$ be the angle at $A$. Solve for $\cos{\theta}$ in surd form.
solution: The right angle is at $B$, so $AC$ is the hypotenuse. For the angle $\theta$ at $A$, the side $AB = {=p}$ is the adjacent side.
Substitute the lengths: $\cos{\theta}=\frac{{=p}}{\sqrt{{=N}}}$. This is the answer in surd form.
notes: Basic tier: all three sides are given (legs whole numbers, hypotenuse a surd), so the student only has to pick adjacent over hypotenuse and write the fraction. No Pythagoras and no cancelling. The book's figure is replaced by a verbal description with fixed vertex names: right angle at B, theta at A, so AB is adjacent, BC opposite, AC hypotenuse. Legs are drawn from 1..5, coprime and unequal, with p^2+q^2 not a square, which leaves 16 ordered pairs (N in 5, 10, 13, 17, 26, 29, 34, 41; all squarefree). Marker has form null on purpose: 1/sqrt(5) and sqrt(5)/5 are the same number and either is correct. Book model ex5-3-2 (cos theta = 5/(5 sqrt 2) = 1/sqrt 2); note the book's printed solution says 'opposite' where it means 'adjacent'. This family uses the correct word.
